hero.title: Language rules, compiler flow, and LSP behavior in one place.
hero.description: This page combines the core J++ language documentation with the practical details that power the editor: strict typing, syntax, compilation, diagnostics, hover, completion, and definition support.

sections.title: J++ Language
sections.summary: J++ is a small strictly typed language that compiles to JavaScript. Its design removes JavaScript-style implicit coercion, so arithmetic and string operations stay predictable.

sections.title: Syntax and Types
sections.summary: The language has two primitive types, number and string. Variables keep the type from their first assignment, and invalid reassignment is rejected at compile time.

sections.title: Compiler Pipeline
sections.summary: Source code flows through a lexer, parser, type checker, and generator before execution. Each phase is isolated so errors stay precise and the implementation stays easy to evolve.

sections.title: LSP Features
sections.summary: The IDE uses a standalone language server over WebSocket to provide diagnostics, hover, completion, definition lookup, and document symbols in near real time.

sections.title: Execution Model
sections.summary: Compiled JavaScript is executed in a constrained sandbox path exposed through the IDE. Compile errors are shown before runtime, and runtime output is streamed back to the UI.

principles.title: Deterministic text
principles.text: . is reserved for string concatenation only.

principles.title: Compile-time feedback
principles.text: Type mismatches are surfaced before execution begins.

principles.title: Stable variables
principles.text: A variable keeps the type from its first assignment.

syntaxExample:
ye a = 5
ye b = 10
ye total = a + b
bol total

ye first = "hello"
ye second = "world"
bol first . " " . second

Source code

compilerStages.title: Lexer
compilerStages.text: Converts source code into tokens and tracks exact line and column positions for diagnostics and editor features.

compilerStages.title: Parser
compilerStages.text: Builds the abstract syntax tree with recursive descent parsing and preserves the structure needed for precedence and blocks.

compilerStages.title: Type checker
compilerStages.text: Infers expression types, validates assignments, manages symbol information, and throws descriptive errors when rules are broken.

compilerStages.title: Generator
compilerStages.text: Emits JavaScript only after the program is known to be valid, keeping code generation intentionally simple.

lspFeatures.title: Diagnostics
lspFeatures.text: Errors are pushed after open and change events, not just after clicking run.

lspFeatures.title: Hover
lspFeatures.text: Keyword docs, operator meaning, and variable type info appear directly in the editor.

lspFeatures.title: Completion
lspFeatures.text: The server returns both keyword suggestions and in-scope variables.

lspFeatures.title: Definition and symbols
lspFeatures.text: Users can jump to declarations and inspect document symbols for faster navigation.

lifecycleSteps: The editor connects to the language server and negotiates capabilities.
The editor sends the full file so the server always has the latest source in memory.
The server runs lexer, parser, and type checking on the current document.
Errors are pushed back to the editor as squiggles and problem entries.
Interactive editor requests are answered on demand.

implementationDetails.title: 0-indexed vs 1-indexed positions
implementationDetails.text: LSP positions are 0-indexed, while the compiler tracks line and column numbers from 1. The server converts values at the transport boundary.

implementationDetails.title: Full document sync
implementationDetails.text: On each change the client sends the full file. That is simpler than incremental sync and is acceptable for small J++ files.

implementationDetails.title: Debounced diagnostics
implementationDetails.text: Diagnostics are delayed slightly so the compiler is not re-run on every keystroke while the user is actively typing.

implementationDetails.title: Shared semantics
implementationDetails.text: The IDE and the LSP server both rely on the same compiler modules, which keeps hover, squiggles, and execution behavior consistent.

runtime.execution: After a successful compile, the generated JavaScript is executed through the IDE runtime path. The user sees compiled output, runtime output, and compile errors in separate views, which makes the pipeline easier to understand while debugging.
runtime.assistant: The chat button on this page uses the documentation retrieval path behind /api/chat. Ask about syntax, operators, compiler behavior, or LSP features to get grounded answers from the project documentation.

documents.title: J++ Language
documents.text: J++ is a small strictly typed language that compiles to JavaScript. It removes JavaScript-style implicit coercion, so arithmetic and string operations stay predictable. The language focuses on deterministic arithmetic, deterministic text handling, compile-time feedback, and stable variable types.

documents.title: Syntax and Types
documents.text: J++ currently supports two primitive types: number and string. Variables keep the type from their first assignment, and invalid reassignment is rejected at compile time. The keyword ye declares variables, bol prints output, agar starts an if condition, nahi defines else, nahi agar adds else-if branches, jabtak creates while loops, ke liye creates counted for loops, tak sets the exclusive upper bound, break exits a loop, and continue skips to the next iteration. The +, -, *, and / operators are numeric only. The . operator is string concatenation only. Comparison operators include ==, !=, <, >, <=, and >=.

documents.title: Compiler Pipeline
documents.text: Source code flows through a lexer, parser, type checker, and generator before execution. The lexer converts source into tokens and tracks line and column positions. The parser builds the abstract syntax tree with recursive descent parsing. The type checker infers expression types, validates assignments, manages symbol information, and reports descriptive errors. The generator emits JavaScript only after the program is valid.

documents.title: LSP Features
documents.text: The IDE uses a standalone language server over WebSocket to provide diagnostics, hover, completion, definition lookup, and document symbols. The editor connects with initialize, sends full-file didOpen and didChange updates, and receives publishDiagnostics notifications after analysis. Hover shows keyword docs, operator meaning, and variable type information. Completion returns keywords and in-scope variables. Definition and document symbols improve navigation. LSP positions are 0-indexed while compiler positions are 1-indexed, and the server converts between them.

documents.title: Execution Model
documents.text: After a successful compile, the generated JavaScript is executed through the IDE runtime path. Users can inspect source code, compiled JavaScript, output, and problems in separate views. The docs assistant uses the /api/chat retrieval path and answers questions about syntax, operators, compiler behavior, and LSP features using the same documentation source.
